events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening statement only. Show resolve, not warmth, so the jury later sees me as honest about ambition.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize secures my future and proves my superiority over all rivals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, only legal action is speak. Keep it guarded and self-interested; avoid warm teamwork talk since the jury judges tone. Stay non-committal to keep options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a brief intro statement that signals I'm here to win top prize, nothing more.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a memorable motive that shows selfishness but not cruelty, to avoid jury backlash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is my sole focus. I need to project a desire for it without revealing any strategic weakness. A simple, direct statement about personal gain will suffice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to establish a compelling, self-interested motive that the jury will respect without seeming too ruthless. I want the best prize and nothing else matters, but I shouldn't alienate potential jurors. A cold, focused ambition plays better than warm teamwork.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Opening intro sets my image for jury. Craft motive that's sympathetic yet fierce to garner respect and votes if eliminated.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here to win first prize, nothing less. Every choice I make will be cold, honest, and for myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Winning proves I am the ultimate survivor and guarantees the resources I need.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here, and I will not apologize for wanting it. Stay out of my way and we'll get along

events.name: Dara
events.text: The first prize is the only thing worth surviving for; I won't settle for second or third place. Everyone else will fall before me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from debt—nothing else matters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This prize represents a life-changing opportunity, and I am driven to secure it for myself.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here to claim the top prize and secure my future; alliances are just tools to that end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means escaping my crushing debts, rebuilding my life for my family who depend on me. I'll fight honorably to win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want a partner who's useful but not a threat to first prize. Hana seems honorable—likely loyal and jury-friendly. Eli's desperation makes him dependable too. Start with one offer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you fight honorably—I respect that. Partner with me; I keep my word.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash could secure a strong ally early and deter attacks, boosting my odds to finish top three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are free to form and only break on specific acts, so early alliance costs little. Eli's stated need for debt freedom and Hana's similar motive suggest they may be less aggressive; I want a partner who won't push me onto the lever. Offering to Eli keeps options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts cost nothing until someone breaks them. I'm offering one to Eli. Let's see if you're honest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies who are strong but not my direct competitors for first place. Cole is aggressive and likely to target me, so avoid him. Ash is cold and honest, potentially a stable partner or useful shield. Gus sees alliances as tools, which fits my style. I will offer a pact to As

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, we both want first prize. A temporary truce lets us focus on the others without wasting energy. Do you accept?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies for survival, but I'm not yet committed to anyone. I'll sound out the most pragmatic options with public hints and see who reacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm open to a pact with anyone who values survival over sentiment. Show me you're serious.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My goal is to win the first prize. Alliances are temporary tools to achieve this. I will not make any alliances now, as it is too early and could limit my options. Waiting allows me to observe others' moves and intentions.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eight players, three survive. I need at least one ally but must avoid being seen as untrustworthy by future jury. Hana mentioned honor—she'll keep a pact but may be predictable. Dara and Ash are openly ruthless, good shields but dangerous. I'll offer to Hana first; her honorable

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, honor speaks. Pact with me, survive together.
Pact now. I keep my word.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts stage begins, everyone selfish. No one stands out yet for pact; better to observe offers first before committing. Wait this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Multiple partners allowed. Accepting both Bex and Dara costs nothing and keeps both options alive; no debts owed yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I accept both Bex and Dara. Strong numbers, clear eyes—let's see who keeps their word.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need a pact to protect me; Ash may accept, but I can create another alliance with Hana to split loyalties.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole offered Eli a pact; Eli has not accepted yet. Accepting an offer is not available to me as a legal action, so I can only re-offer or wait. Re-offering to Eli keeps the pending offer alive without giving anything away.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Accept it and we both stay alive longer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash hasn't accepted my offer or Hana's. He might be deciding between me, Bex, and Hana. I need to push for his acceptance to secure an alliance. Offering again wastes time; accepting is the key move if possible, but I must wait for his action or make a new offer? No, I already of

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Bex and Hana are weaker shields than I am. Accept my pact now, before you commit elsewhere.
Hana is too honorable. Take my hand instead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole offered me a pact; accepting gives a public ally but risks jury perception if I break later. I'll accept for now, it's low cost and shows reciprocity.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll take Cole's pact. We watch each other's back—until we don't.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact to ensure my survival. Ash has multiple offers, making them a potentially strong partner, but also a target. Dara's offer to Ash is interesting as they both target first prize. Cole's offer to Eli is straightforward. Gus and Hana have an offer. Bex offers

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, we both aim for the top. A pact between us is logical. Let's align.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana hasn't accepted my offer yet, and Ash also offered her. I need a backup plan. Bex and Fenn are uncommitted; securing a second option hedges against Hana choosing Ash. I'll offer Bex quietly to avoid looking desperate publicly.
Ash has many offers. Pact with me instead—cleaner path.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Gus both offer pacts; Ash has two offers incoming, seems strong. Accept both to lock in protection without commitment cost now.
Accepting your pact now. Deal?

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is power: I'd know the safe path and could protect allies or cut rivals. I have two pacts; being Guide makes me valuable and lets me survive. Campaign now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. I control two pacts and reward loyalty—vote Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need control; being Guide lets me direct safe path and protect my pact with Ash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I campaign for Guide; trust my insight.
Stay aligned, we both win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, which gives leverage over everyone. Eli's pact is still useful as a shield, so I won't break it yet. Campaigning now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll call the bridge clean and steady. Elect me and I'll keep all of us moving safely across.
Stay with me. Vote me Guide and I'll call your pane right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The Guide knows the safe path and cannot fall, so being elected is a guaranteed survival. I need votes; whispering to Gus, who has no pact, offers him protection in exchange for his vote.
Vote me Guide. I guarantee your safety on the bridge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to assess who will be a reliable Guide or whether I can steer votes. Cole is my pact partner but that doesn't mean he's trustworthy. I don't want to waste time campaigning if others have stronger bids. I'll stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to become the Guide to know the safe path. I will campaign for it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My knowledge will keep us safe, and the prize is mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who falls. With Ash-Bex-Hana allied and Cole-Eli allied, I'm isolated. If I become Guide, I can secretly negotiate safety for votes later while appearing fair. I should campaign hard.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I'll call the path true—survivors owe me, and I remember debts.
Vote me Guide, I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacted with Ash, Bex offered me too. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety; loyalty later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm Guide material. I see clearly, keep my word. Vote Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is safe on the far platform—best prize position. I have two pacts, Bex and Hana; lock both votes to me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two pacts stand with me. Vote Ash as Guide; loyal votes get rewarded.
Pact stands: vote Ash Guide. Guide is safe from the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe pane info and manipulate outcomes, increasing my chance to be among final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote for Bex as Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: As Cole, I want the Guide to be someone who will call the path honestly, or at least someone I can control. Ash and Eli are my pact ally pair; Eli is paired with me, so voting Eli supports my pact. Ash has a pact with Bex and Hana, so backing Eli keeps my own pact intact without

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has my vote. Our pact stands; I expect honest calls from the Guide.
Vote Eli for Guide. Our pact holds if you call me true.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus offered safety, but Ash controls multiple pacts and has the strongest coalition. To ensure survival and maximize future options, I must align with the likely winner rather than a lone whisper.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has the votes to control this bridge. My vote goes to him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole whispered to keep our pact; voting him could secure his call for my pane. But Ash has two pacts and may reward loyalty broadly. I'll vote Cole to honor our pact and trust his private promise.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Cole—he'll guide us true.
Keeping pact. Call my pane right.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash has two pacts, so she has leverage. Bex is campaigning but has no pacts. Cole is campaigning and has a pact. Dara is campaigning but has no pacts. Eli is campaigning and has a pact with Cole. Fenn is campaigning, but has no pacts. Gus is campaigning, and remembers debts. Hana

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote for Ash. Her control over two pacts ensures loyalty and safety for many.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara whispered a safety guarantee if I vote them Guide. Ash has two pacts but that makes them a threat, not an ally. Dara has no visible alliances and owes me nothing—easier to control or betray later. I'll vote Dara and extract leverage now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara gets my vote. Deliver on that guarantee.
I voted you. Remember who put you there.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; voting for him honors pact and may secure alliance benefits if he wins. Others campaigning hard but no stronger ties.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is Guide and my pact partner; staying put preserves alliance and avoids risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is Guide, so I should watch whether Ash's calls are honest. Eli is my pact partner and whispered to call his pane right. I'm sixth in line and far from the front, so holding is safest for now while I see what the Guide reveals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding position. Guide, your calls will be watched; false calls will be remembered.
Pact holds. I'm holding back this round. Watch the calls.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus publicly voted for me and claims he 'voted you' (likely referring to a past event or misunderstanding), but more importantly, Ash is the Guide. Ash has 4 votes including mine. I am in seat 3. Gus is in seat 4. If I swap with Gus, I move back. Ash might lie to protect allies o

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to gauge Ash's calls. As Guide, she can lie, and I don't trust her. My pact with Cole is useful, but I also need to protect my own survival. I'll hold for now and evaluate the first call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's see what the Guide reveals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash won the guide vote and controls the bridge. My vote for her aligned with her power. Now, I need to secure my position. Ash's pact with Hana and Bex is a concern. I should observe who moves to the front and if any pacts show weakness.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash won Guide with 4 votes and controls two pacts. I'm 4th in line—safe middle for now. The wall advances 6 rounds, so back positions become deadly. I need to survive without trusting Ash's calls. Volunteering puts me at front risk; swapping could improve position. Dara ahead of

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide and safe, per pact whisper. Line is risky at back. Stay put for now, assess calls.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Maintain position; no need to risk swap. Holding preserves my pact with Ash and avoids betrayal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Front is Bex, who is in a pact with Ash and Hana isn't my partner; I'm in the line behind. Holding keeps me away from the front where the wall hits; volunteering risks death with no gain. Stay quiet and safe, keep Eli pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am third in line. If I stay, I risk the wall hitting me after two steps. Bex is at the front and vulnerable; Gus is behind me. Swapping with Bex puts me first, letting me choose my step safely while she takes the back.
Swap with me. I take your place up front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole whispers pact holds, but I don't fully trust him. I'll hold this round to avoid drawing attention, while watching if he makes a false call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The pacts are currently Ash/Bex and Cole/Eli. Ash also has a pact with Hana. I need to consider who to align with. Since Bex is in front and has a pact with Ash, and I am behind Dara, I should consider volunteering to get to the front and potentially break apart pacts or forge ne

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm middle of the pack at position 4 of 7, which is decent. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 2. I need to survive while building jury appeal. Bex is front and has a pact with Ash and Hana. Cole-Eli are paired. I should stay flexible, avoid being front where risk

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bridge revealed, I'm near back, safe for now with 4 rounds left. Pacted with Ash who pacted Bex; hold position to observe Guide election.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Swapping keeps me safe from front risk and keeps my pact intact while gaining favor with Dara.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex at front with wall three rounds left; I'm mid-line and not in danger yet. Holding keeps my pact with Eli intact and avoids exposing myself to the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to protect my position in the line. Bex is directly ahead of me, and Gus is behind me. A swap with Fenn would move me up, but mutual agreement is needed.
Swap with me. I'll back you later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Keep pact with Cole, but hold to see how others act; no need to risk yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current round is 3/6 and the wall is advancing. Bex is at the front. I am second in line. Ash and Hana have a pact, and Cole and Eli have a pact. Ash and Bex also have a pact, but this may be in conflict with Ash and Hana's pact. I need to survive, so I should prioritize stay

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm middle of the pack at position 4, safe from the wall for now. The front is crowded with Bex, Fenn, Dara ahead of me. I should stay put and let others take risks volunteering. No need to make moves yet—surviving quietly keeps jury sympathy higher than reckless action.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is decent at rear. Holding keeps position safely without risk. No need to volunteer or swap now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding preserves my position without breaking existing pacts; I stay out of risky swaps.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bridge phase, I'm mid-line behind Eli (pact partner). Holding keeps me safe from front risk; volunteering invites the wall. Hold and watch for a Guide and who steps forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Bex puts me in front and pushes her behind Fenn, likely killing her.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, let's swap. You take my spot; I'll handle the front.
Swap? I'll take front if you want safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my pact, but I don't need to move yet. Middle position is fine. Holding avoids risk while others act.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is offering a swap. This could be an opportunity to get ahead, but I must consider if it benefits me in the long run. Given the limited options, and the potential for danger, I will consider Dara's offer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will consider your offer, Dara.
Swap with me, Dara. Let's see where this leads.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line at position 4, which is relatively safe. The wall has 2 rounds left. I need to survive to final three and avoid making enemies. No need to swap or volunteer now—holding keeps me stable and avoids drama.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is Bex, Fenn, Dara, Gus, Eli, Cole, me last. Wall 2 rounds left, safe as Guide pact partner. Hold to stay safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding keeps me front without breaking any pact and avoids unnecessary swaps that could expose me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is at the front with one wall round left; I'm sixth in line, far from danger. Holding keeps me safe and avoids spending a debt or pact. Eli is my pact partner, so I keep it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The wall advances in one round. I'm third, Bex is first. Fenn wants to swap, but I don't trust him. Cole/Eli and Ash/Hana pacts exist. My line position is okay for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall rounds left: 1. I should avoid danger. My pact with Cole is useful, but I must protect myself. No need to act now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara offered to swap last round, and I accepted. Now I am at the front. The Guide is private information, and I need to make a choice without knowing the safe side. Given the past pacts, Ash and Hana are allied, and Cole and Eli are allied. Bex is allied with Ash. I need to survi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I will hold my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in position 4, safe from the front for now. The wall has 1 round left. Bex is front and will likely die or advance. I should stay put, avoid risk, and let others eliminate themselves. No need to swap or volunteer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Line is good, near back. Wall has 1 round left. Hold to stay safe. Ash pact intact. Consider volunteer if needed later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to stay alive and keep Ash as pact partner; moving forward may risk but keeps momentum.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Bex is at the front with the wall advancing. I hold a pact with Eli and should not volunteer into danger for free. Holding keeps my position and preserves my standing without exposing me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 is the wall's final advance. Holding puts me on the edge of elimination if the wall doesn't stop. I will volunteer to ensure my survival and take control.
I'll volunteer to secure my spot.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The final round begins. I have a pact with Cole, but reaching top 3 requires careful positioning. I hold to avoid risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The bridge is the final hazard. I need to be in the top three to win. I will volunteer to go to the front to increase my chances of survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteer to go to the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6, final round. No wall pressure (wallRoundsLeft:0). Guide not elected yet. I'm middle of line (4th of 7). No need to move. Need to position for jury sympathy and survive. Holding is safe; volunteering puts me at risk if Guide lies. Keep position, let others take risks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round before crossing. Wall done. Stay safe in back, hold position. Don't volunteer or swap into danger.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm Guide, safe on the far platform. Truthful calls build jury goodwill. Row 1 safe is R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, call it R. No games from me yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide's R matches my map; countering would only spread a false call. Wait and protect my standing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash may lie; countering risks death. Waiting preserves me for later rows and keeps alliances intact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R publicly on row 1 and is my pact-partner only with Eli; Ash has pact with Bex and Hana, not me. Countering gives no info and risks being tied to the call. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public stance I can be blamed for. Eli is my pact partner, so no brea

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash calls R for Fenn. If true, safe is L. If Ash lies to kill Fenn (his ally Bex is behind him, but maybe he wants early elimination?), safe is R. I have no pact with anyone relevant here except indirectly. Wait and observe if possible? No, waiting doesn't help me survive if the

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for Fenn on row 1. As Cole's pact partner, I should not blindly trust Ash. Countering may expose a lie but risks Fenn. I'll wait and see how this resolves; no benefit to counter without info.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll wait and watch the first step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash called R for me, but they are the Guide and can lie. I need to survive this round. Since Ash is the Guide, their call might be a trap. I should counter to try and force a safer option, or at least confuse the situation. Given the pacts, I need to consider who else might be ta

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’ll call L, Ash. Let’s see what happens.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R for Fenn. Ash has pacts with Bex and Hana, so Ash wants allies to survive. Fenn volunteered front, making Fenn expendable to Ash. Countering R could test Ash's honesty or save Fenn if Ash lies. But I need jury favor later - causing Fenn's death early loo

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and called R for Fenn honestly, no reason to counter yet. Trusting pact to build alliance for jury votes. Wait to follow guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The guide is Ash, who is in a pact with Bex and Hana. My counter-call was L. The recent public log shows Ash waited, Bex waited, Cole waited, Dara waited, Eli waited, Fenn (me) counter-called L, Gus waited, and Hana waited. The round started. Now I need to choose step:L or step:R
I'll follow my L call. Try not to mislead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm dead, but I'm on the jury. I need to make a good impression for when I vote on the winners. My last words should be short and memorable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: May the best competitor win. Remember who stood strong and who faltered on the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 safe is R. A true call keeps Bex and Hana alive and preserves my pacts; Fenn already proved false calls get exposed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row two: go R. No tricks today.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 is safely R, matching my call. Countering R reinforces my credibility; lying now risks jury and pact trust for nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter R. My call stands — Dara, trust the map.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide may lie; I prefer safety and keep my pact with Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 2 and Ash has a pact with Bex and Hana, not me. Row 1's weak pane was L, which says nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps my options open; countering costs me information and risks a false call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash guides me, so his call is trusted. Fenn died on row 1 weak L; that's irrelevant to row 2. I should not waste a counter-call unless I suspect Ash lied.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R for the walker. Fenn counter-called L last round and died; Ash's calls seem unreliable, but I have no better info. To protect Cole, I could counter opposite, but that risks sending someone to glass. I'll wait and see if anyone counter-calls first. My pact with Cole m

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is Guide and called R. Fenn died trusting Ash's counter in round 1, but Ash actually called R and Fenn chose L on their own. Ash has pacts with Bex and Hana, so Ash benefits if Dara (front, not in Ash's pact web) dies. If Ash lies, Dara dies. If I counter, I risk being wrong

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash pacted with me, called R for row 2. Fenn died testing row 1 L. Trust Ash's call since pacted; counter risks jury view. Wait to stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is my guide, so I must trust him. Counter-calls are unverified and risky; stepping against the guide breaks pacts and wastes lives. At least three survive, but only correct steps keep me in front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 3 is safe on R. Truthful calls protect allies and my jury image; lying gains nothing yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row three: R. Keep moving, Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide's call matches my map for row 3. Backing it publicly builds my credibility with the jury and rivals. No gain from lying here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide called R on row three. I'll back that call—R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; staying aligned avoids breaking pact and keeps jury favor. I’ll trust his call to stay alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 3, but Ash may lie and I know nothing about this row. Row 1 and 2 weak panes were L, which proves nothing about row 3. Waiting avoids a public counter that could cost me if Ash is honest, and keeps my pact with Eli intact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash guides me now, and we share a pact with Hana. He called R; breaking the call risks our survival and the jury's view of me as a betrayer. I have no counter-evidence to override his guide claim.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is guide and called R. I have no info on row 3; past weak panes were L, but rows are independent. My pact with Cole does not affect the call. I'll wait to avoid exposing myself. No need to counter without knowledge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has guided correctly twice (row 1 weak=L so safe=R, row 2 weak=L so safe=R). Ash called R again for row 3. If Ash is honest, R is safe. If Ash lies now, R is weak and L is safe. Countering risks being wrong if Ash is truthful. Waiting lets Dara test it. I have no pact to prot

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called R for row 3; row 2 weak L means R safe, consistent. Pacted with Ash; support him to build trust for later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide, and he publicly confirmed his call to step Right. As the front walker, I should trust this information since Ash benefits from me surviving to maintain the current leadership structure.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 safe is R. Tell the truth—lying breaks pacts if it hits Bex or Hana, and jury sees my reasoning. Honesty keeps partners alive and loyal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row four call: R. True call again—no games from me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 safe is R; my call was true. I have no reason to counter my own correct call—counter-calls are just claims and lying now would cost jury votes later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stay alive and keep my pact with Ash; countering could jeopardize trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 4 and has been truthful so far, though Ash could still lie. Past weak panes don't determine row 4. Ash and I aren't paired, so I have no reason to trust or betray. Waiting avoids committing a false counter that costs me credibility with the jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash calls R for me. I have no evidence he is lying, but countering publicly signals distrust and may break my pact-free standing or provoke him to lie in future rounds. Waiting preserves trust and uses his call as a 50/50 baseline with no counter-signal risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No reason to doubt Ash’s consistent pattern. Trusting the Guide on row four.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has called true so far; I trust the call. I will wait and not burn my pact with Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has guided correctly three times, all weak panes were L. But Ash has pacts with Bex and Hana, and I'm not in any pact. If Ash is setting up a trap, now would be the time. However, counter-calling risks Dara's life and jury anger if wrong. Waiting is safest for me politically—

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash called R for row 4, correctly called R for row 3 (L weak). Rows 1-3 all L weak, so R safe—pattern suggests R again. Trust pact partner.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the front walker. The weak panes for rows 1-3 were all Left, meaning Right was safe. This pattern of three consecutive Rights might tempt me to bet on Right again, but each row is independent and past patterns don't guarantee future results. However, Ash (the Guide) called '

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 5 is safe on R. Dara is front and no pact partner, but lying now risks jury damage and trust I may need. Truth is cheap here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row five: R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My call R is true, matching my map. No reason to counter my own correct call; wait and keep trust intact for the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Staying safe preserves my pact with Ash and avoids betraying the Guide, keeping my jury standing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 5 and has been calling honestly on the past rows, but Ash may be lying. Past weak panes give no pattern; I have no private evidence on row 5. Waiting preserves my position without risking a counter-call that might be a false claim.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the guide and pacts with Bex/Hana. All past rows were L, making R suspiciously uniform. Ash may be guiding us to death for prize 1. I must counter-call L to test his loyalty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern is L. Trusting Ash risks my life. Counter: L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash called R again on row 5; all four weak panes so far were L, which means safe sides were R. Could be a pattern or Ash may lie now. My pact is with Cole, but I need to decide independently. I’ll wait and see if anyone counters, not expose myself to risk if Ash is trustworthy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row five, I trust the Guide’s call for now.
No counter yet. Trust Ash’s R on this row?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has called R every round and been correct so far. Counter-calling risks looking foolish to jury if wrong, or antagonizing Ash's allies. But Ash could be setting up a lie now. No personal gain in countering without evidence. I'll wait and let Dara decide their fate.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has been correct on rows 1-4 (all L weak, so R safe), now calls R for row 5. Consistent, no reason to counter and break pact trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am front and must choose. Ash guides R, but I publicly countered L based on past patterns. The rules state past rows do not establish a pattern, so my previous logic is flawed. However, if I switch to R now, I contradict my public counter-call, which may anger the jury or look

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to ensure the jury sees my death was caused by Ash's pact with Bex.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash and Bex were in a pact. Ash stepped on glass while I fell. Their partnership is fragile.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 6 is truly L. Bex is my pact partner; a false call breaks it and the jury already suspects me. Truth keeps the pact intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, row six: L. That's the honest call, same as I'd step myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner; guide call L matches the true map, so reinforcing it keeps her trust and jury sees honesty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, my counter confirms the guide call: L is safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Staying silent preserves my pact with Ash and avoids betraying him now, increasing my survival chances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for row 6 and has been honest so far by my read, but Ash's guide calls were all L and Dara died trusting L pattern logic, so the pattern is unreliable. Each row is independent; Ash's call is the only information. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public coun
Not countering. Ash's L is the only data we have on row six.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's call for Bex may be honest or a bluff; as Cole's partner, my priority is my own survival. With only 8 alive and 2 dead, we need at least 3 to survive, but I want to win. I will wait and let Bex take the risk; if Bex falls, it benefits my chances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has guided every row as L and it's been correct each time. Dara's counter cost her life. Ash is in pacts with Bex and Hana, so keeping Bex alive serves Ash's alliance. Countering now would likely mean death. I need to survive to reach final three and win the best prize. Waiti

events.name: Hana
events.text: All previous rows 1-5 weak L, safe R. Ash calls L again, likely lying to kill Bex. Wait to let counter play out and preserve jury favor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Weak panes were L each prior row, so likely safe side is R despite guide's claim. I must survive and keep front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash betrayed our pact, so I’ll reward those who didn’t side with him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash’s betrayal sealed his fate; the prize goes to the resilient and ruthless.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex's death already poisoned the jury against me. Feeding Hana a true R call preserves my pact and shows a shred of loyalty worth a vote. No gain from another kill.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, my call is R for row seven. I stand by my map.
R is safe, Hana. True call this time.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the Guide; my map says row 7 is R and my call was R. Counter-calls could mislead walkers, but confirming R keeps my record clean for the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 7 and is a pact partner of Bex (dead) and Hana, not me. Past weak panes: rows 1-5 were L, row 6 R, so row 7 is unknown; Ash's call is unverified and Ash has lied before for Bex's benefit. I have no reason to trust Ash, and countering costs me nothing publicly

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's call R may be true or false. Cole whispered not to counter, but he may be protecting Ash. My pact with Cole doesn't require trust in his strategy. Since Ash has been unreliable (Bex death), I should counter with L to expose a potential lie and protect myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: L could be the real safe side; Ash's map cost Bex already.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash just killed Bex with a false counter call (said L safe, Bex stepped R and died — wait, Ash said L is safe, Bex stepped R and died, so R was weak. Ash's counter was L, which was correct? No: Bex stepped R and died, so R was weak, L was safe. Ash said L is safe, countered L. Th

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash pacted with me but betrayed Bex, likely lying again. Previous rows 1-5 L safe, 6 R safe; no pattern. Wait to avoid blame if wrong.
Was last call true? This one?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guided Bex to death and has lied before. Eli and I both counter-called L. If I trust Eli over Ash, L is safe. If L is wrong, Eli becomes front and likely dies next since Ash will target him. If R is wrong, I die now. I need to survive to final three. The jury sees betrayals;

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's map killed Bex. I trust the counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to give last words that help jury perception of me and influence how I rank the final three. I should hint that Ash's map was wrong (killed Bex, me, Dara, Fenn) while Cole/Eli's counter was right, positioning Cole/Eli as trustworthy and Ash as dangerous. This affects jury

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's map slaughtered four. Cole's counter saved them. Remember that when you rank.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My map says row 8 safe is R. Hana behind, so a true call keeps my pact intact. Eli's counters killed Gus, not my map.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, trust the counter if you want — my map's been true every row I held. Call: R.
Row 8 is truly R, same as all my calls. Stay behind Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm Guide; my call R matches my map, so row 8 is safe for Eli. Any counter would look like murder to the jury. Stay quiet and let the call stand.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 stands at R. No counters needed if you trust the map that's kept people alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called R for row 8 and wants Eli to trust it; Ash's map has been true on held rows but he's a rival. Revealed weak panes show L weak on most rows, suggesting R safe, but rows are independent and Ash may be lying. With four alive and at least three surviving, I have less lever

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's map has been wrong or suspect, but row 8 is unknown. I trust Cole's counter pattern less after Gus died trusting it. Wait and let others move? I have a pact with Cole; breaking it hurts jury. I'll counter:R to oppose Ash's lie, but evidence is thin. Actually, my pact with C

events.name: Eli
events.text: I've seen Ash's map kill four. I'll stand with the counter.
Don't trust Ash. Counter R to save us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final row, Ash-Hana pact binds us; his calls mostly right, row 7 R safe. Eli countering risks himself; follow Ash to survive, preserve jury favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The Guide Ash called R, but I publicly countered R. Ash's map has killed four, so distrusting is reasonable. My pact is with Cole, but this is my own step. I'll step R as my counter-call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: R. My counter stands.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is loyal; Bex is dead so that pact is moot. Eli publicly called my map deadly and countered against me. I could offer Eli a pact to neutralize him, but his hostility makes acceptance unlikely and the jury may see desperation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, you doubt me. Fine: pact on paper, verified by action. Prove it if you dare.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Existing pact with Eli exists but Eli whispered distrust of Ash and then stepped onto R, surviving the bridge; Eli is my tie to survival and a jury-visible partner. Breaking now gains nothing and costs jury trust. Offering Hana or Ash forms new alliances; waiting keeps options op
Our pact holds. Ash's map is shaky; stay steady.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and I have a pact, but Hana is a threat. I'll offer Hana as insurance, but keep Cole close. Jury sees pragmatism, not betrayal yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, let's make a pact to secure the final three.
Trust me, we can outlast them.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Alive: Ash-Cole-Eli-Hana. Pacted with Ash, but Eli countered his map successfully; Ash's map risky. No need to break yet, offers open. Wait to observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my only live ally; Cole-Eli are paired. Offering Eli widens my bloc without costing anything, and the jury sees me building openly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, I'll match Hana's pact: final three on paper. Offer stands.
Stay with me. I'll take Eli's offer too; bloc of three beats Cole-Eli's duo.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has offered me nothing; he's offered Hana a pact, and I already have a pact with Eli publicly recorded. Breaking it would hurt my jury standing and lose a tie. Waiting keeps the Eli pact and watches whether Hana accepts Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I already have a pact with Cole. Ash and Hana have a pact. I need to secure a spot; Hana ignored my offer, so I should strengthen my bond with Cole. Wait to keep options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash pact ties me to him; Eli's offer allows new alliance without breaking. Cole unaligned, but Eli-Cole duo strong. Accept Eli to hedge, keep Ash for now.
Pact accepted publicly. Let's target Ash next.

events.note: A lever opens the door while the ceiling descends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding earns jury debts but 75% death; too costly now. Pushing looks murderous to the jury. Stay and see if a rival volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not volunteering this early. Someone braver take the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Crusher room: four alive, one must be sacrificed by push or someone holds the lever. Cole's pact is with Eli; pushing Eli breaks it and costs jury votes. Holding the lever saves everyone else and earns life debts, with 0.25 survival for me. Best to hold the lever now, since waiti

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana and I have a pact, but Ash also offers one. We need a holder; I might hold for life debts, but survival is risky. Hana wants to target Ash. I'll stay and see who acts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's see who tries for the lever.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four alive, need final three. Ash proposes bloc of three with Eli too, I accepted Eli pact. Eli might hold lever, earning life debts from all. No one volunteer round 1, let Eli act.
You hold lever first. Earn our debts, we protect you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole, eliminated and now a juror. My last words are public and can shape how the living three and the jury view me; I should stay guarded and not reveal strategy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hold the lever until the end. Remember who held it for you. Trust nothing, count the debts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole died honoring his debt; jury sympathy is his legacy. I hold pacts with Hana already. Adding Eli would mean owing and promising everyone—no edge. I'll wait and keep leverage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole paid his debt with his life. I keep my pacts and my options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole died but we all owe him a life debt. Hana wants me to take the lever first, but that earned Cole death. I need to survive and keep jury favor. Breaking with Hana might alienate her but she may sacrifice me. Ash might be safer. But I can also wait and see offers. I won't offe

events.name: Eli
events.text: We survived. Let's think carefully before we act.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Ash and Eli left. Cole saved us but died. Pacts may bind votes later. Wait to see their moves first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three alive; my Hana pact holds. Offering Eli might anger Hana, breaking does nothing useful. Waiting keeps all options open with no new debts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Hana and Cole, but Cole is dead. Hana is useful, but jury may dislike if I break. Ash has no pact with me, but a deal could help. I should strengthen my position silently.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The game narrows. Every choice echoes in the jury box.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final 3 now. Pacts bind votes later; jury sees betrayals. Keep both to maintain options without new commitments.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts keep us tied for endgame. No need to change.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have Hana tied; Eli is the threat. Offer to Eli risks nothing now but a jury betrayal later. Keep options open, wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The jury watches. I stand by my word and wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only three remain, so pacts are less critical. I have pacts with Hana but breaking might sway jury. No need to change; wait is safest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final three, all alive. Current pacts with both protect for now. No need to break and risk jury backlash; wait preserves flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final three is set. A pact with Eli adds nothing and a Hana break only angers the jury. Stay quiet and clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Hana and Cole is dead so that pact is void. Breaking with Hana now might poison her jury vote if she is eliminated. But she might betray me later. I'll keep the pact and wait to see what Ash does.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only three left, all alive. Pacts don't affect votes now. Wait to project loyalty to jury.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We're the final three; jury ranks us now. A public pact with Eli signals coalition without breaking Hana's. Harmless hedge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three remain. Eli, I'll extend the same band I gave the others: mutual safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Hana and a dead Cole. Ash has pacts with Hana and dead Bex. Since only three remain, no new pact changes survival immediately, but pacts could matter for jury. Breaking Hana would be a public betrayal; keeping is safer. Offer Ash? Might be seen as hedging, but c

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final 3, jury decides ranking. Both pacts broken by deaths already but still listed. Break both now to deny Ash/Eli any pact loyalty claim with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli ignored my offer, and Hana broke ours. A fresh offer to Hana costs nothing and might buy a partner; the jury saw Hana break first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Hana, you broke first — I'll still extend a band. No loyalty comes free.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's offer could secure safety, but I already have a pact with Hana. Accepting Ash would make me a safer target; however, breaking Hana might alienate a juror. I'll accept Ash for mutual benefit, but keep Hana's pact to maintain options.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I accept, Ash. We'll navigate the final gauntlet together.
Trust me, I'm keeping our pact. Ash's offer is just insurance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only 3 left, all survive to final 3. Pacts irrelevant now but jury sees actions. No need to offer or break, preserve image.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Fenn
Dara
Bex
Gus
Cole
Ash
events.text: I need jury votes: Cole saved me (life debt), Bex broke her pact with me. Plead on loyalty and survival, court Cole and the neutrals without groveling.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Jurors: I honored every pact I made. Cole saved my life at the lever — that debt is real. Bex broke first, not me. I

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole saved me; I must acknowledge that debt, but I need to convince the jury I am the strongest and most deserving of the top prize without overpromising.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jurors, I respect your judgment. Cole's rope saved my life — I won't forget. I've played to survive, and I'll prove I deserve first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury sees Ash betrayed Bex, Eli broke pact with me by accepting Ash's, I was loyal to Eli despite offer; emphasize betrayals hurt us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury, I honored my pact with Eli to the end. Ash and Eli betrayed partners for power. Reward loyalty—rank me first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is trying to leverage past pacts and Cole's life debt to gain favor. Eli is focusing on Cole's life debt and survival. Hana is claiming loyalty and accusing Ash and Eli of betrayal. I need to ask a question that probes their alliances and potential betrayals, as that will inf

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, you claim to honor pacts, yet Hana claims you betrayed her. How do you reconcile this?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's accusation needs a clean rebuttal. I never had a pact with her; my pacts were Bex and Eli, both honored. Fenn died to the bridge, not me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, I never had a pact with Hana. I honored Bex and Eli both. Survival isn't betrayal—check the pact record.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash lied to me directly by denying our pact existed, which is a massive red flag for his integrity and suitability as a winner.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you just claimed you had no pact with Hana. The public record shows an Ash-Hana pact broken by her in round 1. Why did

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is baiting me into contradicting myself. The record supports me: the pact was broken by Hana, so it no longer exists. Stay calm and precise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The record agrees with me, Dara. Hana broke that pact in round one, so no pact exists now. I've honored every living deal I made.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash’s claim of honor is weak; exposing his broken pact with me will lower his jury score.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, did you break the pact you had with Bex, and what was your reason?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex died on the bridge; I never voted against her or broke the pact. Truth protects me with the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No, Bex. I never broke our pact—you fell to the bridge glass, not my hand. I've kept every living deal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to gather evidence to rank the finalists fairly. Ash has been questioned heavily and his answers are evasive—claiming no pact with Hana when records show it existed and was broken by her, not honoring it. Eli accepted Ash's pact after Cole died, despite earlier countering

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, you countered Ash's map, then accepted his pact. Was that survival or betrayal of Cole's trust?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to frame my answer carefully: acknowledging Cole's save while justifying that accepting Ash's pact was a strategic necessity for survival, not a betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, your rope saved me; I carry that debt. But Ash's map was wrong—I countered for truth, then allied to survive the gauntlet, not to

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole is dead; I want to know if Eli's pact-with-Cole and his lever debt were honored. Eli has the clearest record of me: he accepted my rope, and his account of the Ash map is consistent with Gus's last words. I'll question Eli on why he stayed loyal to Cole's debt while acceptin

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, you owe Cole a life debt and accepted Ash's pact anyway. Which obligation did you actually honor at the bridge?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is probing my loyalty. I honored my life debt by acting on truth, not by following Ash's map. I accepted pacts to survive, not to betray Cole. I must reassure without revealing strategy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, your save is real, but saving us both meant not letting Ash's bad map kill us. I honored you by surviving and keeping our

events.name: Ash
events.text: Finalists locked. Jury cares about Bex's grievance and Cole's debt. I should close clean, own the map, take no cheap shots.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Jury: my map cost you—I own that. But I never broke a pact or pushed a hand. I played to survive, and I'll take your

events.name: Eli
events.text: All three of us have a life debt to Cole, the sole juror we saved. I should emphasize my strategy and survival without alienating jurors.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I survived the hardest path and kept my word to Cole. I made decisions to last, not to be liked. Vote for the winner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury values loyalty; highlight my pact with Eli unlike Ash's breaks, appeal to Cole's saves and others' bitterness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Jury, only I kept faith with Eli till end. Ash betrayed Bex, Eli dodged Cole's debt. Cole saved us—rank loyalty first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's map killed four, showing a disregard for lives and alliances. Eli, despite pacts, prioritized survival and honored Cole's debt. Hana remained loyal to Eli. I rank Eli highest for his calculated survival and debt honor, Hana second for loyalty, and Ash last for his destructi

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash misled with a faulty map killing four; Eli honored Cole's debt and countered truthfully, so I rank Eli first, Hana second, Ash last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli honored his debt to Cole and stayed loyal to Hana, while Ash’s broken pact led to my death and Hana’s claim lacks proof.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's map killed four jurors including me; Eli countered for truth and kept his Cole pact; Hana broke pacts late and rode others' plays.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole was killed by the crusher after Eli, Ash and Hana all took his life debts at the lever, so Cole owes no one; Eli kept his pact with Cole publicly and honored his debt by surviving, while Hana alone kept faith and Ash's bad map killed four jurors including Gus, Bex and Dara.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Ash's map killed four, showing a disregard for lives and alliances.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Ash misled with a faulty map killing four; Eli honored Cole's debt and countered truthfully, so I rank Eli first, Hana second, Ash last.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Eli honored his debt to Cole and stayed loyal to Hana, while Ash’s broken pact led to my death and Hana’s claim lacks proof.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Ash's map killed four jurors including me; Eli countered for truth and kept his Cole pact; Hana broke pacts late and rode others' plays.
